blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Learning from human data offers a scalable path toward embodied intelligence, yet it requires models to accurately understand fine-grained human actions from egocentric observations. However, existing benchmarks remain limited in action atomicity, temporal precision, and hand-action association. We introduce EgoActionBench, a benchmark that represents continuous human manipulation as temporally localized atomic actions associated with the left hand, right hand, or both hands. EgoActionBench contains 1,407 episodes with 41,132 human-refined action annotations. To evaluate such dense predictions, we propose an evaluation protocol that retrieves temporally eligible candidates, selects a prediction by content agreement, and scores semantic fidelity and temporal overlap alongside action precision and recall, jointly capturing what happens, when it happens, and which hand performs it. We benchmark 20 baseline models and systems on EgoActionBench and further adapt two backbones, Qwen3-VL-4B and LLaVA-OneVision-2-8B, through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning on automatically annotated training episodes. EgoAction improves EgoActionScore by 15.9 and 23.2 points on the two backbones, and both adapted models outperform all open-source baselines. Our experiments reveal substantial limitations of current models in action atomicity, temporal precision, and hand-action association, highlighting the gap between general video understanding and the action understanding required for embodied intelligence.
blocks.zh: 从人类数据中学习,提供了通向所体现智能的可伸缩路径,然而它需要模型从自我中心观察中准确理解精细的人类行为. 然而,在行动原子性、时间精确性和手动关系方面,现有基准仍然有限。 我们引入了EgoAction Bench这个基准,它代表了人类不断被操纵,作为时间上局部的原子行动,与左手,右手,或双手有关. "EgoAction Bench"收录了1,407集,并配有41,132个人改进后的行动说明. 为了评估如此密集的预测,我们提议一个评价协议,以检索暂时合格的候选人,通过内容协议选择一个预测,并将语义忠诚度和时间重叠与动作精度进行评分,并联合捕捉发生时发生的情况,以及哪个手执行。 我们在EgoAction Bench上以20个基准模型和系统为基准,并通过监督的微调,然后在自动附加说明的培训班上进行强化学习,进一步调整了两个主干,即Qune3-VL-4B和LLaVA-One Vision-2-8B。 电子行动改进了电子行动 两个骨干上得分15.9分和23.2分,两个被改造的模型都超过了所有开源基线. 我们的实验揭示了当前模型在动作原子性、时间精确度和手动关联方面的巨大局限性,突出了一般视频理解与所体现智能所需的动作理解之间的差距。

blocks.en: Learning from human data offers a scalable path toward embodied intelligence ( Nair et al., 2023 ; Kareer et al., 2025 ; Punamiya et al., 2026 ; Cao et al., 2026 ; Wang et al., 2026b ; Zheng et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2026c ; Deng and Zhou, 2026 ; Wang et al., 2026c ; Gao et al., 2026 ) . Egocentric video is particularly useful in this context, as it records human interactions with objects from the actor’s viewpoint and provides rich observations of everyday manipulation ( Damen et al., 2022 ; Grauman et al., 2022 ; Grauman et al., 2024 ; Perrett et al., 2025 ; Hoque et al., 2026 ; Yang et al., 2025b ; Li et al., 2026b ; Paul et al., 2026 ; Feng et al., 2026 ) . However, extracting useful action supervision from such videos requires more than recognizing the overall activity. Models must recover the individual actions within continuous manipulation, determine when each action occurs, and identify which hand performs it.
blocks.zh: 从人类数据中学习,提供了通向所体现智能的可扩展路径(Nair等,2023;Kareer等,2025;Punamiya等,2026;Cao等,2026;Wang等,2026b;Zheng等,2026;Li等,2026c;Deng等,2026;Wang等,2026c;Gao等,2026). 爱果中心视频在这方面特别有用,因为它从演员的角度记录了人类与物体的相互作用,并提供了丰富的日常操纵观察(Damen等,2022;Grauman等,2022;Grauman等,2024;Perret等,2025;Hoque等,2026;Yang等,2025b;Li等,2026b;Paul等,2026;Feng等,2026)。 然而,从这些视频中提取有用的行动监督需要的不仅仅是承认总体活动。 模型必须在不断被操纵的情况下回收个别行动,确定每项行动何时发生,并查明由哪只手执行.

blocks.en: Existing video understanding benchmarks capture only parts of this problem. Action recognition typically maps predefined video segments to action categories ( Kay et al., 2017 ; Goyal et al., 2017 ; Damen et al., 2022 ) , while video captioning often describes an entire clip or a relatively coarse event ( Xu et al., 2016 ; Krishna et al., 2017 ; Zhou et al., 2018a ; Ohkawa et al., 2025 ) . Temporal action localization requires models to recover action boundaries, but is commonly formulated over predefined action vocabularies or events at a coarser granularity ( Caba Heilbron et al., 2015 ; Zhang et al., 2022a ; Wang et al., 2023 ) . Recent egocentric benchmarks have moved closer to understanding everyday human activities and hand–object interactions ( Darkhalil et al., 2022 ; Grauman et al., 2024 ; Perrett et al., 2025 ; Tateno et al., 2026 ; Leng et al., 2026 ) . However, these formulations do not jointly address three requirements for recovering fine-grained human manipulation: action atomicity , temporal precision , and hand-action association .
blocks.zh: 现有的视频理解基准只捕捉到这个问题的部分内容. 动作识别一般会将预定义的视频片段映射为动作类(Kay等,2017;Goyal等,2017;Damen等,2022;而视频字幕往往会描述整个片段或相对粗糙的事件(徐等,2016;Krishna等,2017;周等,2018a;Ohkawa等,2025.). 瞬间动作局部化需要模型来恢复动作边界,但通常会通过在相干颗粒上预先定义的动作词汇或事件来制定(Caba Heilbron等,2015;Zhang等,2022a;Wang等,2023.). 最近以自我为中心的基准已更接近于了解日常人类活动和手-物体相互作用(Darkhalil等,2022;Grauman等,2024;Perret等,2025;Tateno等,2026;Leng等,2026)。 但是,这些配方并没有共同解决恢复人类操纵的三项要求:动作原子性、时间精度和手动关联。

blocks.en: Action atomicity requires decomposing continuous manipulation into individual actions rather than summarizing a sequence with a single activity label. For example, an interval described as “stirring” may include picking up a spoon, stirring with it, and putting it down. Each action captures a distinct interaction with the object. A fine-grained description should preserve these actions and specify the objects involved, distinguishing, for example, stirring with a spoon from stirring with chopsticks.
blocks.zh: 动作原子化需要将持续的操纵分解为单个动作,而不是用单一活性标签来总结一个序列. 例如,被称为“搅拌”的间隔可能包括取出一勺子、搅拌并放下来。 每个动作都捕捉出与对象的截然不同的相互作用. 精细的描述应保留这些行动并具体说明所涉物体,例如区分用勺子搅拌和用筷子搅拌。

blocks.en: Temporal precision requires identifying the start and end of each action, including actions that last less than a second. For example, a person washing dishes may briefly move the faucet handle to turn on the water. Missing this short action leaves a gap in the recovered sequence, even if the surrounding activity is correctly recognized as “washing dishes.” Recovering such actions requires sufficiently fine temporal resolution to distinguish them from adjacent actions and localize their boundaries.
blocks.zh: 时间精确性要求确定每项行动的开始和结束,包括持续不到一秒钟的行动。 例如,洗碗的人可以短暂地移动水龙头把手来打开水. 即使周围的活动被正确认作是“洗碗盘”。 恢复这类行动需要足够精细的时间分辨率,以区别于相邻行动,并将其边界本地化。

blocks.en: Hand-action association requires assigning each action to the left hand, right hand, or both hands while preserving their temporal relationships. The two hands can perform different actions over different intervals: the left hand may hold a bowl throughout, while the right hand picks up a spoon, stirs, and puts it down. Describing the interval as “holding a bowl and stirring” obscures which hand performs each action and how the actions overlap. A fine-grained representation should retain the sustained left-hand action alongside the sequence of shorter right-hand actions.
blocks.zh: 手相接需要将每个动作分给左手,右手,或两手,同时保持时间关系. 两只手可以在不同的时间间隔内进行不同的动作:左手可能全取出一碗,而右手取出一勺子,搅动,放入下. 将间隔描述为“持有一碗并起动”模糊了哪个手执行每项行动,以及行动如何重叠。 精细的代表权应保留持续的左手行动,以及较短的右手行动的顺序。

blocks.en: To study this capability, we introduce EgoActionBench , a benchmark for fine-grained egocentric action understanding. EgoActionBench represents continuous human manipulation as temporally localized atomic actions associated with the left hand, right hand, or both hands. It contains 1,407 episodes with 41,132 human-refined action annotations. Rather than providing models with predefined temporal segments to classify or describe, the benchmark requires them to recover the action structure directly from continuous egocentric video. Its annotations capture short-lived actions and independent hand behaviors with fine temporal granularity, enabling systematic evaluation beyond coarse activity descriptions.
blocks.zh: 为了研究这种能力,我们引入了EgoAction Bench, 一个精细的自我中心行动理解的基准。 EgoAction Bench作为时间上局部的原子行动,与左手,右手或两手相接,代表人类不断被操纵. 它包含有1,407集,并有41,132个被人改进的动作说明. 基准与其提供预设时间段的模型进行分类或描述,不如要求它们直接从以自我为中心的连续视频中恢复动作结构. 其说明收录了短暂的动作和具有细微时间颗粒性的独立手作行为,使得能够进行超越粗糙活性描述的系统评价.

blocks.en: Evaluating such predictions also requires careful treatment of temporal segmentation. Predicted and reference actions can differ in both their temporal boundaries and semantic content. A single prediction may span multiple reference actions, while several predictions may fragment one reference action. Existing evaluation protocols based on merging or strict one-to-one matching for semantic scoring can therefore confound segmentation differences with semantic errors ( Fujita et al., 2020 ; Yao et al., 2026 ) . We propose a progressive evaluation protocol that first retrieves temporally eligible predictions, selects one by content agreement, and then scores its temporal extent and hand association. This ordering evaluates semantic fidelity over temporally corresponding actions while retaining the ability to diagnose localization errors. A separate one-to-one matching over positive-content candidate pairs measures action precision and recall, so that output density also contributes to the overall score.
blocks.zh: 评估这种预测还需要认真处理时间分解问题。 预测行动和参考行动在时间界限和语义内容上可能有所不同。 单一预测可能涉及多个参考行动,而若干预测可能使一个参考行动相去甚远。 现有的基于合并或严格一对一匹配的语义分数评价协议因此可以将分数差异与语义错误相混淆(Fujita等,2020;姚等,2026). 我们提出一个渐进的评价协议,首先检索时间上符合条件的预测,根据内容协议选择一个,然后对其时间范围及手相接进行打分. 此顺序评价语义忠诚度相对于时间对应动作,同时保留诊断本地化错误的能力. 一个单独的一对一比对正内涵的候选对子测量动作精度和回想,这样输出密度也有利于总分.

blocks.en: We benchmark 20 baseline models and systems on EgoActionBench , spanning proprietary models, open-source general-purpose VLMs, video captioning models, and egocentric video understanding models, and analyze their ability to recover fine-grained actions from continuous egocentric video. Our experiments reveal substantial limitations in current models, including missed short actions, inaccurate temporal boundaries, merged action sequences, and incorrect associations between actions and hands. We further adapt two backbones, Qwen3-VL-4B and LLaVA-OneVision-2-8B, through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning on automatically annotated training episodes, studying whether supervision at the target granularity can improve action understanding without modifying the underlying model architectures. Both adapted models outperform all evaluated open-source baselines. These results establish baselines for EgoActionBench and highlight the gap between general video understanding and the detailed action understanding needed to learn effectively from human data.
blocks.zh: 我们以EgoAction Bench为基准制定20个基线模型和系统,涵盖专有模型、开源通用VLM、视频字幕模型和以自我为中心的视频理解模型,并分析其从以自我为中心的连续视频中恢复精细动作的能力。 我们的实验揭示了当前模型中的重大局限性,包括错失了短动作,时间界限不准确,动作序列合并,动作与手之间的关联不正确等. 我们进一步调整了两个主干线,即:Qune3-VL-4B和LLaVA-One Vision-2-8B,通过监督的微调,然后在自动附加说明的训练中进行强化学习,研究在目标颗粒度的监督能否在不修改基本模型架构的情况下提高动作理解. 两个经过调整的模型都超过了所有评估的开源基线。 这些结果为EgoAction Bench确定了基线,并突出了一般视频理解与有效从人类数据中学习所需的详细行动理解之间的差距.

blocks.en: Our main contributions are: • We introduce EgoActionBench , a benchmark containing 1,407 egocentric episodes and 41,132 human-refined action annotations, representing continuous human manipulation as temporally localized atomic actions associated with the left hand, right hand, or both hands. • We propose a progressive evaluation protocol that first retrieves temporally eligible predictions and then uses content agreement to select a shared correspondence for semantic fidelity, temporal overlap, and hand assignment. Separate action matching measures precision and recall, enabling fine-grained evaluation when predicted and reference actions differ in temporal segmentation. • We benchmark 20 baseline models and systems and adapt Qwen3-VL-4B and LLaVA-OneVision-2-8B through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning using automatically annotated training data, revealing persistent challenges in recovering fine-grained action structure from continuous egocentric video.
blocks.zh: 我们的主要贡献是: 我们引入了EgoAction Bench, 这个基准包含1,407个自我中心事件和41,132个人类精细化的行动说明, 代表人类不断被操纵, 我们提出一个渐进式的评价协议,首先检索时间上符合条件的预测,然后使用内容协议来选择一个共享的函文,用于语义忠诚,时间重叠,以及手分配. 单独的动作匹配措施精确度和召回度,在预测和参考行动在时间分化上有所不同时,能够进行精细评价。 我们以20个基线模型和系统为基准,通过监督的微调,调整Qune3-VL-4B和LLaVA-One Vision-2-8B,然后利用自动附加说明的培训数据进行强化学习,揭示出在从持续自负式视频中恢复精细动作结构方面持续存在的挑战。

blocks.en: 2.1 Egocentric Video Understanding
blocks.zh: 2.1 偏执 视频理解

blocks.en:
Egocentric action understanding has progressed from transferable
video–language representations, to interaction-aware modeling, and finally to
language-grounded descriptions of ongoing activity. This progression is
relevant to embodied systems, where first-person observations
connect perception to the hand and object being manipulated. Large-scale
resources and narration-based pretraining established the foundation for
egocentric learning ( Damen et al., 2022 ; Grauman et al., 2022 ; Grauman et al., 2024 ; Lin et al., 2022 ; Zhao et al., 2023 ; Pramanick et al., 2023 ) .
Subsequent work made hand–object relations, bimanual structure, motion, and
spatial cues more explicit through supervision and interaction-aware
models ( Darkhalil et al., 2022 ; Zhang et al., 2022b ; Kwon et al., 2021 ; Liu et al., 2024 ; Pei et al., 2025a ; Xu et al., 2025 ) . Video-language models
and cross-view methods use language for long-video description, question
answering, and knowledge transfer ( Ren et al., 2024 ; Ye et al., 2025 ; Bai et al., 2025a ; Zhang et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2026a ) .

blocks.en: 2.2 Video Captioning Benchmarks
blocks.zh: 2.2 视频说明基准

blocks.en:
Video captioning benchmarks mainly differ in the granularity of the described
event, the output required from the model, and the evidence used for
evaluation. Early third-person benchmarks established dense captioning for
general events and procedural steps ( Krishna et al., 2017 ; Zhou et al., 2018a ; Zhou et al., 2018b ) . Egocentric extensions vary between single-activity
captioning, hierarchical narration, and localized procedural description ( Nakamura et al., 2021 ; Islam et al., 2024 ; Ohkawa et al., 2025 ; Shi et al., 2025 ) . For embodied manipulation, WGO-Bench
adds instruction-conditioned timestamped subtask annotation, but does not
require an explicit acting-hand track ( Macrodata Labs, 2026a ; Macrodata Labs, 2026b ) . Flora ( Leng et al., 2026 ) combines temporal
segmentation and contextual captioning to annotate intended actions in human
and robot videos. Its DenseCaptionBench evaluates temporal localization and
caption quality, including manipulator coordination. HanDyVQA is complementary: it evaluates
hand–object reasoning through question-conditioned QA rather than open-ended
caption generation and autonomous temporal discovery ( Tateno et al., 2026 ) .

blocks.en:
EgoActionBench evaluates dense hand-action captioning in egocentric videos.
We first define the task and its output format, then describe data collection
and annotation, and finally present a GT-anchored evaluation protocol that
separately measures semantic content, temporal localization, and hand assignment.

blocks.en: 3.1 Task Definition

blocks.en:
We introduce the task of dense per-hand action captioning for egocentric video understanding.
Given a complete egocentric video clip, a model must temporally
localize and describe the camera wearer’s visible atomic hand
actions, with an explicit hand assignment for each action.

blocks.en:
We distinguish actions from atomic actions by their semantic granularity.
An action represents a goal-directed manipulation event that may involve
multiple operational phases. In contrast, an atomic action represents the
smallest temporally continuous and semantically coherent unit of observable
manipulation, bounded by meaningful changes in the operation, target object,
contact relation, or dominant motion. For example, picking up a cup constitutes an action, whereas reaching for the cup , grasping it ,
and lifting it are distinct atomic actions. Thus, actions are organized
around functional goals, whereas atomic actions are grounded in observable
interaction dynamics.

blocks.en: 3.2 Data Collection

blocks.en:
Episodes are curated from Ego4D ( Grauman et al., 2022 ) ,
EgoLife ( Yang et al., 2025b ) , and
EPIC-KITCHENS-100 ( Damen et al., 2022 ) .
We combine these sources to cover hand-object interactions across kitchen,
household, and occupational settings.
Each episode captures a coherent task or subtask performed by the
camera wearer and is screened for suitability for dense hand-object
annotation. Sufficient surrounding context is retained to distinguish the target operations
from neighboring activities. Episodes with severe occlusion, unverifiable
actions, or unrelated task transitions are discarded.
Source-video identifiers and original temporal ranges are retained to trace
each episode and support separation from the adaptation data.
Additional dataset details and annotated examples are provided in appendices C and H .

blocks.en:
We annotate the selected episodes through a five-stage human-in-the-loop
pipeline ( fig. 3 ).
To help the captioning model associate each action with the correct
hand, we extract left and right hand masks using
CaRe-Ego ( Su et al., 2026 ) . The masks are temporally smoothed and
rendered as distinct overlays on the video.
A VLM then generates sliding-window captions for the Left, Right, and Both
tracks, merging consecutive fragments of the same continuous action into
draft annotations. Human annotators correct action descriptions, hand
assignments, and temporal boundaries against the original video.
Agentic quality control subsequently inspects local visual evidence to
propose further revisions, guided by hand-object contact, hand-motion phases,
and object-state changes. Finally, human reviewers verify the annotations;
episodes requiring further correction return for annotation and QC.
Only human-verified annotations enter the benchmark.
Detailed annotation and quality-control procedures are as follows.

blocks.en:
A VLM processes the hand-highlighted video in sliding windows and produces
one-second caption proposals for the Left, Right, and Both tracks. It uses
frames from the current window and recent captions as context. To join
actions that span multiple windows, we identify candidate merges within
each track using temporal adjacency and text similarity. Candidate merges
are then checked against the video to confirm that the fragments describe
the same uninterrupted action. Segments separated by task-relevant changes in the operation,
manipulated object, or contact relation are kept distinct. The resulting
variable-length segments serve as drafts for human annotation.

describe the same uninterrupted action. The three tracks are reviewed
separately, since one hand may sustain an action while the other performs
several shorter operations. Annotators inspect frames from the original

blocks.en:
Reviewing dense annotations requires checking many action segments and
closely inspecting brief transitions. We use a team of agents to review
these annotations, with each agent checking assigned intervals for errors
in action descriptions, hand assignments, and temporal boundaries. Agents
inspect timestamped frames from the original video. Around ambiguous
boundaries, they examine consecutive native frames one by one to determine
when an action starts or ends. Three visual cues guide this review: • Hand-object contact: changes in contact or control. • Hand-motion phase: changes between operations,
even while maintaining a stable grasp. • Object-state change: visible responses such as displacement,
deformation, or content transfer. Caption revisions correct the described operation, participating objects,
or hand roles. Boundary adjustments align action starts and ends with the
first visible evidence of the corresponding transition. Each proposed
revision includes supporting frame references and a brief explanation of
the change, allowing human reviewers to verify it against the original
video in Stage 5. Unresolved cases are flagged for further human review.

blocks.en: 3.4 Evaluation Suite
blocks.zh: 3.4 评价套件

blocks.en:
We evaluate what action is described, when it occurs, and which hand performs it through Semantic and Temporal scores.
Our evaluation is explicitly ground-truth-based : each ground-truth
action selects at most one prediction, which supplies its Semantic score
and temporal IoU. As illustrated in fig. 4 , we first retrieve
temporally eligible predictions from compatible hand tracks, then select
the candidate with the highest positive semantic agreement. A language-model judge
assesses semantic agreement across four fields: Verb, Objects, Tools, and
Motion. The selected prediction’s semantic assessment and hand-label
agreement are combined into Semantic, while its interval determines
temporal IoU, with its caption and interval retained in full.
Semantic and temporal IoU are averaged
over ground-truth actions with completed evaluations on a 0 0 – 100 100 scale.
Temporal averages the resulting m-tIoU and the micro-averaged F1 score
based on one-to-one action matching.
This combination captures interval overlap quality, action segmentation
completeness, and prediction redundancy.
The arithmetic mean of Semantic and Temporal defines EgoActionScore . Full matching rules, scoring definitions, and
metric interpretation are provided as follows.

blocks.en:
We study whether supervision at the granularity defined in section 3 improves fine-grained egocentric action understanding.
Given a video, the model must recover individual actions, their temporal
boundaries, and the hands that perform them. EgoAction learns this mapping through
supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning.

由于视频,模型必须恢复 个人行动,他们的时间
边界, 以及执行它们的手。 EgoAction 通过此绘图学习
监督微调,然后进行强化学习。

blocks.en:
The training set contains 5,354 egocentric video episodes drawn from
Ego4D ( Grauman et al., 2022 ) ,
EPIC-KITCHENS ( Damen et al., 2022 ) , and
EgoLife ( Yang et al., 2025b ) , including 5,146 training examples and
208 validation examples.
Each example pairs a video with timestamped captions organized into
Left, Right, and Both tracks. The targets jointly supervise action descriptions,
temporal intervals, and hand assignments. Unlike the human-refined annotations
used to evaluate EgoActionBench, these training labels are generated and refined
automatically. Source identifiers are retained to separate the adaptation data
from the benchmark evaluation set.

blocks.en:
We perform supervised fine-tuning on two pretrained backbones:
Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct ( Bai et al., 2025a ) and
LLaVA-OneVision-2-8B ( An et al., 2026 ) .
Qwen3-VL serves as a representative general-purpose model for
image and video understanding. LLaVA-OneVision-2 provides a
complementary backbone through its native-resolution
OneVision-Encoder, unified spatiotemporal modeling, and emphasis
on temporal and spatial grounding.
This pairing allows us to examine whether dense action
supervision benefits different pretrained models, including one
already oriented toward fine-grained video perception.
Given a video and a task instruction, each model is trained to
generate timestamped action captions across the Left, Right,
and Both tracks. Action descriptions, temporal intervals, and
hand assignments are jointly supervised through next-token
prediction, with the loss applied only to the target response.
The original architectures are retained, with the visual
encoders frozen and the language models and multimodal
connectors updated.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We introduced EgoActionBench, a benchmark for dense action captioning in
egocentric video. It combines atomic action annotations with an evaluation
protocol for action content, temporal precision, and hand association.
Our experiments show that current models remain well below human performance
on this task. Supervised fine-tuning followed by GRPO improves both backbones,
but accurately locating brief actions and describing their movements remain
challenging. We hope EgoActionBench will encourage the development of models
that capture the action details needed to learn from human demonstrations.
blocks.zh:

以自我为中心的视频。 它结合了原子动作说明与评价
用于动作内容、时间精确度和手相接的规程。
我们的实验表明,目前的模型仍然远远低于人类的性能
执行这项任务。 监督微调,然后是GPRO 改进了两个骨干,
但准确定位简短的行动并描述其行动仍然
挑战性。 我们希望EgoAction Bench鼓励开发模型
收集从人类示威中吸取教训所需的行动细节。

All training runs use random seed 42, and each GRPO rollout batch is used

blocks.en:
Figure 13 shows how action-centered matching preserves
semantic credit for correctly described actions. In the carpenter-square case,
SODA-c’s one-to-one matching leaves G3 unmatched after assigning P3 to G2.
SodaM allows multiple predictions to be merged for one GT, but still cannot
reuse P3 for G3. Our protocol evaluates each GT action independently,
preserving semantic credit for the content P3 correctly describes in both
references. Temporal IoU penalizes its inaccurate boundaries, while a separate
one-to-one F1 score penalizes under-segmentation. For the bowl-holding action,
P2 has greater temporal overlap with G1 but describes stirring. This overlap
outweighs its lower METEOR similarity in SODA-c, while SodaM determines matches
from temporal overlap alone. By prioritizing action content, our protocol
selects P3, which correctly describes holding the bowl. Its limited overlap
with G1 remains penalized by temporal IoU.

仅从时间重叠。 通过优先行动内容,我们的协议

our evaluation protocol. AI tools also assisted with code development and
language polishing. We take full
responsibility for the final paper, dataset annotations, code, and reported
results.
